target_moa.text: Ioflupane I 123 binds reversibly to the dopamine transporter (DaT) on dopaminergic neurons concentrated in the striatum; radioactive decay of iodine 123 emits gamma radiation allowing SPECT visualization of the striata, reflecting DaT density.

citations.quote: In vitro*, ioflupane binds reversibly to the human recombinant dopamine transporter (DaT) (K_i = 0.62 \text{ nM}; \text{IC}_{50} = 0.71 \text{ nM}).

Following administration of DaTscan to humans, radioactive decay of the iodine 123 emits gamma radiation which can be detected externally using gamma detectors, allowing visualization of the brain striata through SPECT imaging
DaTscan is a radiopharmaceutical indicated for striatal dopamine transporter visualization using single photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) brain imaging
The active drug substance in DaTscan is 123I-ioflupane, a cocaine derivative with affinity for the DaT.

key_safety.text: No serious adverse reactions in clinical trials; most common adverse reactions (headache, nausea, vertigo, dry mouth, dizziness) each occurred in <1% of subjects. Hypersensitivity and injection site reactions have been reported post-marketing.

citations.quote: In clinical trials, the most common adverse reactions, headache, nausea, vertigo, dry mouth or dizziness occurred in < 1% of subjects. (6.1)
No serious adverse reactions were observed in the clinical trials and adverse reactions were uncommon (<1% of patients).
Hypersensitivity and injection site reactions have been reported following DaTscan administration. (6.2)
